title: The Delinquent and the Transfer Student
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Riri, a cheerful transfer student, makes a game of getting Atsuko, the school's feared sukeban (girl-gang delinquent), to say cute words from her lists. The game becomes an excuse to spend time together, and the two high-school girls' friendship slowly turns into a first romance. Database tags place it in 1980s Showa-era Japan.
life_message: Looking past a frightening reputation, and being gently honest about one's feelings, opens the way to real affection.

content.note: Atsuko is known as the school's top fighter; the review describes no specific fights.
Atsuko's scary reputation is played for comedy.
Same-sex romance between two high-school girls; MangaUpdates lists a first kiss; MangaDex rates it safe; reviewer calls it very gentle.
Rough gang slang is central; the reviewer says the English edition softens it.
Delinquent image is affectionate and comic, not glamorized crime.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Atsuko's fighting reputation matters to her gang, but the story values gentleness over defending face.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Atsuko chooses her time with Riri even when her second-in-command objects (Okazu review).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Gang loyalty versus a new bond; family barely features beyond tagged accepting parents.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Gang ranks exist but the romance crosses the feared-leader and newcomer divide.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: No religious frame; personal feeling guides choices in a 1980s setting.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Cute-word game, open same-sex romance and accepting parents put self-expression first.

folkways.japan: The sukeban girl-gang image and senpai-style gang ranks draw on 1980s Japanese youth subculture, recalled here with nostalgia rather than as a social problem.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer describes a cute, low-stakes romance carried by the word game; no speeches noted (to verify).
delivery.note: The romance is presented as natural and sweet without arguing for or against anything.

winners_losers: Riri and Atsuko both win: the feared delinquent finds tenderness and the newcomer finds belonging. Sympathy goes to self-expression and acceptance.
